Seminar Title:

Multiphysics 4D Printing: Development and Investigation of Stimuli-Responsive Structures for Soft Robotic Actuation

Seminar Type:

Registration Seminar

Department:

Mechanical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Saumyaranjan Tripathy ( Rollno : 525me1011)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

ME001: ME Dept Seminar Hall

Date and Time:

15 Oct 2026 11.15 AM

Contact:

Saroj Kumar Patel

Abstract:

Four-dimensional(4D) printing goes beyond conventional additive manufacturing by producing structures that can change their shape or function when subjected to an external stimulus. The present research focuses on the development of responsive 4D printed structures in which material behaviour, structural design, and controlled actuation are considered together. As an initial stage of the work, polylactic acid (PLA) structures were printed using fused deposition modelling (FDM) while a graphene nanoplatelet (GNP)-based conductive composite was prepared and deposited over the PLA structure using direct ink writing (DIW). The conductive region was introduced to provide localized heating through Joule effect when an electrical voltage was applied. The morphology, electrical response, electrothermal heating behaviour, and the thermally activated shape-memory responses of the printed structures were investigated. The results showed that the deposited PLA/GNP composite formed an electrically conductive path and generated heat under electrical stimulation exhibiting shape recovery of the printed part. The future research will investigate the relationships among material composition, fabrication parameters, structural geometry, stimulus conditions, and resulting deformation through experimental characterizations and multiphysics modelling. The work will subsequently be extended toward additional modes of stimulation, intelligent control, and adaptive actuation, with the aim of developing programmable 4D printed structures for soft robotics application.

Keywords: Four-dimensional(4D) printing, Shape-memory polymers, Fused deposition modelling (FDM), Direct ink writing (DIW), Joule heating, Adaptive actuation.
